Skew-normal regression with bias reduction

snreg.Rd

Fits the linear model \(y_i = x_i^\top\beta + \varepsilon_i\) or the partially linear model \(y_i = x_i^\top\beta + f(t_i) + \varepsilon_i\), with \(\varepsilon_i \sim SN(0, \sigma, \alpha)\) independent, by one of four methods:

`"ML"`

maximum likelihood; the shape estimate is reported as `Inf` or `-Inf` when the likelihood has no finite maximizer (see [sn_mle()]).

`"CS"`

the corrective estimator \(\hat\theta - b(\hat\theta)\) with the Cox and Snell bias \(b\) ([sn_bias()]).

`"mean"`

the mean bias-reducing adjusted score estimator (Firth, 1993), always finite in our experience.

`"median"`

the median bias-reducing adjusted score estimator (Kenne Pagui, Salvan and Sartori, 2017); linear models only.

With a smooth term only `"ML"` (penalized likelihood) and `"mean"` are available; see [snplm()].

Usage

snreg(
  formula,
  data,
  smooth = NULL,
  method = c("mean", "median", "ML", "CS"),
  k = 10L,
  lambda = NULL
)

Arguments

formula

model formula for the location (linear part).

data

data frame.

smooth

optional name (character) of a covariate entering through a P-spline term.

method

one of `"mean"`, `"median"`, `"ML"`, `"CS"`.

k

basis dimension of the smooth term.

lambda

optional fixed smoothing parameter.

Value

An object of class `"snbr"`.

Examples

fit <- snreg(logit_clay ~ depth, data = arcticlake, method = "mean")
summary(fit)
#> snreg(formula = logit_clay ~ depth, data = arcticlake, method = "mean")
